title: Custom type kinds (catalog)
hook: You do not only get `int` and `string`. The language offers several type constructors. This is a map, not OOP — inheritance and members come later.

sections.heading: What you can declare
sections.prose: class — reference type, identity, later inheritance. struct — value type, copies, no class-style inheritance. record class / record struct — compiler-grown equality, `ToString`, `with`. interface — contract, no storage of its own. enum — named integers. delegate — typed method group (later). tuple — `(string id, int n)` without a named type. generic types — `List<T>`, placeholders. These are how you model an SQS envelope (class/record), a RGB color (struct), a cache policy enum, and a `(score, weight)` pair while parsing CSV. Pick from the catalog using size and identity: if two instances with the same data should be interchangeable, start with record or struct; if identity and lifecycle (SkiaSharp `SKSurface`) matter, class plus dispose later.

snippets.label: Catalog, not a full OOP lesson
snippets.explanation: Interview: name the kinds and one reason to choose each. Do not dive into virtual dispatch until module 05.

interviewTakeaways: class vs struct is reference vs value, not “big vs small” alone — but small + copy is the struct heuristic.
records add value-based equality; they are still class or struct.
tuples are unnamed; promote to a type when the pair leaks across methods.
commonPitfalls: Mutable structs in collections — copies bite.
Enums for open-ended string issuers from auth providers — a class or constants may fit better.
Treating interface as a type that can be `new`ed.

jsTsCorrelations.note: TS interfaces and type aliases erase. C# interfaces remain in metadata. TS `enum` can emit runtime objects; C# enums are value types.
